commands.exec: Run a console command in the views

errors.bad_args: The console got arguments it cannot read: {reason}
errors.expression_too_long: The command is longer than {limit} characters.
errors.mcp_exec_off: Running console commands over MCP is off. A person can switch it on in Settings > DevTools & Debugging > Console > Commands over MCP; the console panel's command line works without it.
errors.no_active_view: No view is active; run the command in all views instead.

panel.commandHint: A JavaScript expression, run in the views' isolated world; Enter runs it.
panel.noCapture: The console receives nothing yet: the app does not hand this plugin the views' messages.

bufferSize.description: How many messages the console keeps per view; older ones drop out.
bufferSize.help: How many messages the console keeps per view; older ones drop out. Raise it for pages that log a lot, lower it to save memory.
bufferSize.label: Messages kept per view

clearOnNavigate.description: A view's messages from before its last navigation leave the console.
clearOnNavigate.help: Messages from before a view's last navigation leave the console, so each page starts clean. Off keeps them across navigations.
clearOnNavigate.label: Clear on navigation

execTarget.description: Where a command of the console's command line runs unless the panel says otherwise: in every view or only in the active one.
execTarget.help: Where a command from the console's command line runs unless the panel says otherwise: all views, or the active one only.
execTarget.label: Run commands in

levels.description: The levels the console panel shows when it opens: Errors, Warnings, Info, Logs, Debug and Network.
levels.help: The levels the console panel shows when it opens; the rest are hidden until you tick them. Example: Errors and Warnings only for a quiet review.
levels.label: Levels shown

mcpExec.description: Lets an AI agent run JavaScript in the views through the MCP tool sharedconsole_exec. Off by default; the panel's command line works either way.
mcpExec.help: Lets an AI agent run JavaScript in the views through the MCP tool sharedconsole_exec. Keep it off unless an agent needs it; the panel's command line works either way.
mcpExec.label: Commands over MCP

networkLevel.description: Which fetch and XHR requests appear at the level Network: none, the failed ones (an error status or no answer) or all of them.
networkLevel.help: Which fetch and XHR requests show at the Network level: off none, errors the failed ones (error status or no answer), all every request.
networkLevel.label: Network requests

showRbrowserMessages.description: Shows what rBrowser's own plugins reported in a view (a failed request of the rulers, say), marked with the source rBrowser and the plugin. Off by default: they are no messages of the page, and the rBrowser log has them either way. A plugin's page script that failed shows either way, with its stack.
showRbrowserMessages.help: Shows what rBrowser's plugins reported in a view, marked rBrowser and the plugin's name, beside the page's own messages. Off keeps the console to the page; the rBrowser log keeps them either way. A plugin script that failed always shows, with its stack.
showRbrowserMessages.label: rBrowser's own messages

tools.exec: Runs a JavaScript expression in the targeted views (isolated world) and answers one result per distinct value, with the views that gave it. Off until a person allows it in the settings (Console > Commands over MCP).
tools.grouped: The shared console: the views' console messages, uncaught exceptions and failed fetch/XHR requests, deduplicated (numbers and ids ignored) with the views that reported each and how often. Optional levels, views, search and limit filter; clear: true clears the console after answering.
